scenario: AITA for refusing an additional guest at our wedding | Thanks for watching this post. First time writing here and non-native English speaker. I am getting married very soon. As you can imagine, this takes a lot of preparation. I'm talking here about the civil wedding, which will be very intimate and consequently restricted to our very close family: parents, siblings and, in my case, godparents and their children. The wedding will happen in another country, so this takes a lot of preparation as it is in another culture. When I made the invitations, I've been clear: I invited my parents (2 p.) and my godparents' family (4 p.). I've been very flexible, I told everyone that they could join us anytime they like (i.e., arrive in the country when they wish because I understand it's complicated when you have 4 different jobs etc) as long as they'll be present for the ceremony. Moreover, because the destination is far, my in-laws kindly proposed to offer the accommodation to all of them. The wedding is now in one month and I just received a message from my godmother saying that they have booked the flights, and they will be 5 because the gf of my cousin is joining. That's where I am really feeling uncomfortable: I receive this as a 'fait accompli' (done deal) without any prior consultation, without even asking me if that's ok to have an additional person (that I've never met). I've always been clear about the number of people invited. I just can't stand to receive this kind of 'news' via a late evening text message. It's not that I'm against that additional person. It's just the way that I'm put in front of this, as if I had nothing to say. And we're not talking about the 'party' wedding, but something very special that is meant to be in strict intimacy. Moreover, I know that they have their tickets since 1 month, and I was waiting for their news to plan the trip etc. So they literally waited 1 month to announce it, now that the date is getting closer. I just don't understand this kind of behavior. It costs nothing to make a quick phone call before booking anything, and to ask if it's possible, etc. In sum, they just invited someone at my wedding, someone that wasn't ever planned and that I don't even know. This morning, I sent a polite message saying: 'I'm confused by your news, I've always been clear about the number of guests and why I picked these specific guests (i.e. you) for our wedding. Why haven't you called me and asked me before booking anything? I'm put in front of a done deal, and I have to oppose myself to it, as it goes against the very idea of what we've been planning for months. The solution to this situation, I am afraid, does not lie within my hands. If X is feeling uncomfortable about this, I could understand, but with respect to my in-laws, I just cannot accept this compromise.' So: Am I the asshole? More precisely: Am I the asshole for refusing this, for writing to them clearly that it will not be possible and that they should have contacted me before doing anything? Thanks.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what's going on here. I'm getting married soon, and it's a civil wedding that's supposed to be very intimate. That means only our very close family is invited: parents, siblings, godparents, and their children. Since the wedding is in another country, it's a lot of work to organize everything, especially because it's in a different culture. When I sent out the invitations, I was clear about who was invited. I invited my parents (2 people) and my godparents' family (4 people). I was also flexible, telling everyone they could come anytime they wanted, as long as they were present for the ceremony. Plus, my in-laws offered to provide accommodation for everyone, which is really kind. Now, just one month before the wedding, I received a message from my godmother saying that they've booked their flights and that there will be 5 people instead of 4 because the godfather of my cousin is joining them. This is where I feel really uncomfortable. It feels like they're making a decision without consulting me, as if I have no say in the matter. It's not that I'm against having an additional person; it's just the way it's being presented to me, as if I have no opinion. I've always been clear about the number of people I wanted to invite, and I picked these specific guests for a reason. I can't stand receiving this kind of "news" via a late-night text message. It's not about the person they're bringing; it's about the lack of communication and consideration for my plans. They waited a whole month to announce this, and now that the date is getting closer, it's like they're springing it on me. It would have cost them nothing to make a quick phone call before booking anything and ask if it's possible. Instead, they just invited someone to my wedding without my knowledge or consent. This morning, I sent a polite message expressing my confusion and frustration. I explained that I've always been clear about the number of guests and why I picked these specific people. I asked why they didn't call me before booking anything and pointed out that they're presenting me with a done deal, which goes against everything we've been planning for months. I also mentioned that the solution to this situation doesn't lie with me and that if my partner is uncomfortable, I could understand, but I can't accept compromising on this. So, the question is: Am I the asshole for refusing this additional guest and for clearly stating that it's not possible and that they should have contacted me before making any arrangements? First, I need to consider the context. The wedding is supposed to be intimate, and I've been clear about the guest list from the beginning. It's understandable that I want to keep it that way, especially since it's in another country and requires a lot of planning. On the other hand, my godparents are adding someone to the guest list without consulting me. They waited a month to tell me, which seems like poor communication. It's also a bit presumptuous to assume that I would be okay with an additional guest, especially someone I don't know. I'm feeling frustrated because I feel like my boundaries are being ignored. I've been clear about the guest list, and they didn't respect that. It's not just about the number of guests; it's about the lack of consideration for my plans and feelings. However, I also need to think about how I responded. I sent a polite message explaining my feelings, but I also made it clear that I couldn't compromise on this. Is that being reasonable, or is it being too rigid? I guess it's reasonable to want to keep the guest list as planned, especially for an intimate wedding. But maybe I could have communicated my feelings more calmly or tried to find a compromise instead of outright refusing. But then again, if the guest list was clearly defined from the beginning, and they're adding someone without my consent, it's understandable that I would feel upset and want to maintain my boundaries. In the end, I think it's not necessarily being an asshole to refuse the additional guest and to express my frustration. It's more about how I communicate my feelings and whether I'm open to finding a solution that works for everyone. Maybe I could have approached the situation with a bit more understanding and willingness to discuss the issue instead of immediately refusing. But given the circumstances, I can see why I would feel the way I do. So, in conclusion, while it's important to stand up for what I want, especially regarding something as personal as my wedding, it's also crucial to communicate my feelings in a way that's respectful and open to dialogue. That way, I can maintain my boundaries without coming across as inflexible or unkind.
